subject: Acme - Integration & Prompt Governance follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Integration & Prompt Governance follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side:

Call summary:
- Primary use case: customer support assistant that combines knowledge base retrieval + structured tool calls (ticket creation/update).
- Traffic profile: pilot ~5k queries/day, median input 300 tokens, 95th perc OK at 1k tokens.
- SLOs: 300ms p50, 800ms p95 for generation after retrieval.

Integration / architecture notes:
- SDK setup: you can use the Redwood JS SDK for rapid prototyping. We'll share a sample repo (attached redwood-sdk-setup.md) that shows streaming + function/tool calling.
- Auth: recommend short-lived API keys from your SSO + optional mTLS for Dedicated/private deployments. For hosted we suggest token rotation and per-environment keys.
- Routing & fallbacks: plan to route low-latency requests to a small gen-optimized model, fallback to higher-quality model for reranks. We can supply model profiles for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Structured output & tool calling: use function-calling with a strict JSON schema; Redwood can validate post-generation and reject on schema mismatch. We'll prototype ticket_create/ticket_update functions in the workshop.
- Embeddings & rerankers: we recommend our embeddings hosted endpoint for freshness; use dense re-ranker on top of BM25 for highest precision. We can provide an evaluation baseline.

Prompt templates & governance (high level):
- Versioning: store prompt templates in a versioned registry (we can demo a simple Git-backed approach + prompt metadata: version, owner, intent, test-cases).
- Injection mitigations: recommended layers: 1) strict system prompt that enforces task & role, 2) input sanitation, 3) output schema validation, 4) prompt red-teaming to discover edge cases.
- Red teaming: propose an initial red-team pass using adversarial prompt lists + automated fuzzing. We'll map findings to mitigation tickets and unit tests.

Action items / next steps:
1) Share SDK setup + architecture stub (attached). — Marissa (done)
2) Schedule 90-min workshop to align on auth, routing, and prompt governance (propose Tue/Wed next week). — Alex to confirm
3) Provide sample dataset for embeddings eval (Acme to share anon export). — Alex
4) Redwood to draft prompt governance playbook + initial red-team checklist (we'll attach v1). — Marissa / Dylan

Attachments: acme-integration-architecture-stub.pdf, redwood-sdk-setup.md, prompt-governance-playbook-v1.pdf

Thanks — happy to iterate on the agenda.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. This looks great. A couple clarification questions before the workshop:

1) Prompt versioning: are you relying on Git tags only, or does Redwood provide a registry that enforces schema and test-case gating on deploy?
2) Red-teaming: curious how you quantify coverage and severity for prompt injection findings — do you provide severity levels and suggested mitigations?

We can do Tue 4/15 at 10am PT for the workshop. Also we'll try to share a sanitized export of 1k support tickets by EOD 4/14.

—Alex

Head of Product
Acme Corp
alex.j@acme.com

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Integration & Prompt Governance follow-up

Perfect — thanks Alex. Quick answers and proposed workshop agenda below.

Answers:
- Prompt registry: Redwood provides a lightweight registry (we'll demo) that layers on top of Git. It enforces metadata (version, owner, intent) and configurable pre-deploy checks (unit tests, prompt evals, schema compatibility). Teams can keep prompts in their existing repo and push via CI.
- Red-team severity & coverage: we tag findings with severity (low/med/high) and map to mitigations. Coverage metrics are currently: unique injection classes discovered, fail-rate on unit tests, and percentage of templates with automated tests. We can share a sample taxonomy.

Workshop (90m) proposed agenda (Tue 4/15, 10:00–11:30 PT):
- 10:00–10:10 Intro & goals — Marissa
- 10:10–10:30 Auth & deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated/private) — Dev
- 10:30–11:00 Integration demo: SDK + function-calling + validation (live) — Dylan
- 11:00–11:20 Prompt governance: registry, versioning, and red-team process — Marissa
- 11:20–11:30 Next steps & action items

I'll attach the prompt governance playbook v1 and a short README for the SDK. See attachments in my previous email.

If that time works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Best,
Marissa

Looping back with the infra plan for the workshop/demo environment so we're aligned on prep: 

- Demo environment: gen-optimized model in us-west with a small Dedicated pool to meet p50 target; a high-quality model in fallback. We'll pre-provision a sandbox API key for Acme and restrict r/w to the demo project.
- SDK examples: I'll wire up the ticket_create function with strict JSON schema and a small mock backend for side-effects (we'll surface the webhook config).
- Embedding eval: Marissa, please confirm the sample payload size (Alex mentioned ~1k tickets). We'll run a small recall/precision sweep and deliver a short report during the workshop.
- Prompt registry: I'll prepare example prompt versions (v1, v1.1) and a failing unit test example (injection case) to demo gating.

Attachments: acme-demo-infra-plan.md

On Tue I'll bring the infra plan and we'll iterate live.

—Dylan
